category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #1 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old male presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_b: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_c: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_d: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_e: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #2 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_b: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_c: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_d: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_e: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #3 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_b: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_c: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_d: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_e: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #4 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_b: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_c: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_d: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_e: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #5 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_b: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_c: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_d: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_e: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #6 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_b: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_c: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_d: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_e: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #7 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 38-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_b: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_c: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_d: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_e: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

option_a: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_b: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_c: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_d: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_e: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #208 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_b: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_c: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_d: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_e: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #209 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old male with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, he develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_b: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_c: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_d: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_e: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #210 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_b: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_c: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_d: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_e: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #211 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 38-year-old female presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_b: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_c: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_d: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_e: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #212 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 86-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_b: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_c: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_d: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_e: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #213 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old male presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_b: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_c: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_d: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_e: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_b: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_c: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_d: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_e: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #267 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_b: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_c: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_d: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_e: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #268 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old male presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_b: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_c: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_d: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_e: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #269 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 86-year-old male presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_b: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_c: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_d: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_e: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #270 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old male presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_b: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_c: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_d: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_e: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #271 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_b: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_c: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_d: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_e: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #272 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_b: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_c: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_d: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_e: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

option_a: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_b: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_c: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_d: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_e: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #355 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_b: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_c: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_d: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_e: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #356 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old male with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, he develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_b: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_c: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_d: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_e: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #357 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_b: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_c: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_d: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_e: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #358 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old female presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_b: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_c: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_d: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_e: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #359 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 46-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_b: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_c: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_d: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_e: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #360 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old male presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_b: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_c: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_d: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_e: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_b: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_c: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_d: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_e: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #414 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old male presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_b: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_c: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_d: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_e: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #415 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 38-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_b: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_c: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_d: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_e: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #416 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old male presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_b: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_c: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_d: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_e: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #417 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old male presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_b: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_c: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_d: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_e: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #418 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_b: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_c: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_d: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_e: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #419 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_b: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_c: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_d: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_e: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_b: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_c: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_d: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_e: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #620 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 38-year-old female presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_b: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_c: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_d: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_e: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #621 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 46-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_b: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_c: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_d: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_e: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #622 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_b: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_c: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_d: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_e: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #623 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_b: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_c: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_d: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_e: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #624 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 86-year-old female presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_b: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_c: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_d: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_e: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #625 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_b: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_c: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_d: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_e: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

option_a: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_b: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_c: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_d: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_e: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #679 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 46-year-old female presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_b: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_c: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_d: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_e: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #680 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old male presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_b: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_c: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_d: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_e: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #681 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 38-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_b: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_c: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_d: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_e: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #682 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_b: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_c: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_d: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_e: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #683 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old male presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_b: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_c: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_d: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_e: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

question: Question #684 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 86-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_b: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_c: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_d: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_e: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

option_a: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_b: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_c: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_d: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_e: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #973 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_b: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_c: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_d: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_e: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #974 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 86-year-old male presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_b: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_c: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_d: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_e: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #975 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_b: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_c: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_d: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_e: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #976 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_b: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_c: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_d: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_e: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #977 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old male presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_b: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_c: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_d: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
option_e: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #978 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_b: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_c: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_d: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_e: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
option_b: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_c: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_d: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_e: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #1061 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_b: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_c: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_d: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_e: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #1062 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
option_b: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_c: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_d: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_e: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #1063 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
option_b: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_c: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_d: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_e: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Infectious Disease (Cardiothoracic Surgery)
question: Question #1064 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 46-year-old male presents with a 5-day history of high fever, severe retro-orbital headache, diffuse myalgias ('breakbone fever'), rash, and petechiae. Lab analysis shows thrombocytopenia (45,000/mm3) and leukopenia. Serology confirms flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.
option_a: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_b: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_c: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
option_d: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_e: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #1065 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old female presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
option_b: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_c: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_d: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_e: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #1066 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
option_b: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_c: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_d: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_e: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

option_a: Leptospirosis causing Weil syndrome with hepatic hemorrhage and renal failure
option_b: Dengue fever with risk of dengue hemorrhagic fever due to antibody-dependent enhancement
option_c: Plasmodium falciparum malaria characterized by cyclic schizont rupture and merozoite release
option_d: Rickettsia rickettsii infection causing Rocky Mountain spotted fever vasculitis
option_e: Chickungunya virus infection characterized strictly by chronic destructive arthritis
explanation: Dengue fever is a flavivirus transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, presenting with fever, retro-orbital pain, severe myalgias, and thrombocytopenia. Secondary infection with a different serotype increases risk of severe dengue via antibody-dependent enhancement.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Cardiovascular (Trauma)
question: Question #1149 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 63-year-old male presents with acute shortness of breath, orthopnea, and paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea. Physical exam demonstrates bilateral pulmonary crackles, elevated jugular venous pressure (12 cm H2O), and an S3 gallop. Echocardiogram shows ejection fraction of 28%.
option_a: Combination therapy with ARNI (sacubitril/valsartan), evidence-based beta-blocker, aldosterone antagonist, and SGLT2 inhibitor
option_b: Monotherapy with high-dose sublingual nitroglycerin and immediate oral beta-blocker loading
option_c: Discontinuation of all antihypertensive medications and administration of IV digoxin alone
option_d: Placement of an intra-aortic balloon pump prior to diagnostic cardiac catheterization
option_e: Immediate surgical mitral valve replacement as first-line non-pharmacological therapy
explanation: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, EF <= 40%) is managed with 4 foundational pillar therapies: ARNI/ACEi/ARB, beta-blockers (carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, bisoprolol), MRA (spironolactone), and SGLT2 inhibitors.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Renal & Endocrine (Acute Abdomen)
question: Question #1150 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 79-year-old female presents with profound weakness, weight loss, hyperpigmentation of palmar creases and oral mucosa, and orthostatic hypotension. Lab values show serum sodium 128 mEq/L, serum potassium 5.9 mEq/L, morning plasma cortisol 2.1 mcg/dL, and elevated plasma ACTH.
option_a: Secondary adrenal insufficiency due to pituitary corticotroph adenoma apoplexy
option_b: Cushing syndrome secondary to ectopic ACTH-secreting small cell lung carcinoma
option_c: Inappropriate ADH secretion (SIADH) resulting from paraneoplastic lung syndrome
option_d: Primary hyperaldosteronism caused by adrenal cortical zona glomerulosa adenoma
option_e: Primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) caused by autoimmune adrenalitis
explanation: Primary adrenal insufficiency presents with low cortisol, high ACTH (causing hyperpigmentation via MSH co-cleavage), hyponatremia, and hyperkalemia (due to concomitant aldosterone loss).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pulmonology (Biliary Surgery)
question: Question #1151 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 30-year-old female presents with progressive dyspnea on exertion and dry cough. High-resolution chest CT shows subpleural reticulation, honeycombing, and traction bronchiectasis predominantly at lung bases. Pulmonary function testing demonstrates restrictive pattern with reduced DLCO.
option_a: IgE-mediated allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis with central bronchiectasis
option_b: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis driven by GM-CSF receptor autoantibodies
option_c: Usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern characteristic of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
option_d: Acute eosinophilic pneumonia secondary to environmental allergen exposure
option_e: Diffuse alveolar damage caused by acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)
explanation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) exhibits the UIP pattern on HRCT (basilar subpleural honeycombing and traction bronchiectasis) with restrictive lung physiology and decreased DLCO.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Gastroenterology (Vascular Surgery)
question: Question #1152 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 71-year-old female presents with severe epigastric abdominal pain radiating straight to the back, relieved by leaning forward, accompanied by persistent nausea and vomiting. Lab testing shows serum lipase 1,450 U/L (normal < 60 U/L). Abdominal ultrasound demonstrates a dilated common bile duct with choledocholithiasis.
option_a: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy for autoimmune pancreatitis
option_b: Immediate exploratory laparotomy for total pancreatectomy and splenectomy
option_c: Oral ursodeoxycholic acid administration for 6 months without endoscopic intervention
option_d: Empiric prophylactic IV vancomycin and meropenem prior to diagnostic imaging
option_e: Initial aggressive IV fluid resuscitation, bowel rest, analgesia, and ERCP for gallstone removal
explanation: Acute gallstone pancreatitis requires aggressive fluid resuscitation, pain control, and early ERCP if choledocholithiasis or cholangitis is present.

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Neurology (Urology)
question: Question #1153 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 54-year-old male presents with recurrent episodes of neurologic deficits separated in time and space, including optic neuritis (painful unilateral vision loss) and Lhermitte sign (electric shock sensation down spine on neck flexion). Brain MRI reveals periventricular white matter demyelinating lesions (Dawson fingers).
option_a: Guillain-Barré syndrome caused by peripheral nerve demyelination following Campylobacter infection
option_b: Myasthenia gravis caused by autoantibodies against postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors
option_c: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis causing degeneration of anterior horn cells and corticospinal tracts
option_d: Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease driven by neuronal spongiform degeneration and prion accumulation
option_e: Multiple sclerosis characterized by autoimmune demyelination of central nervous system axons
explanation: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune demyelinating disease of the CNS characterized by dissemination in time and space. Brain MRI classically shows periventricular demyelinating plaques (Dawson fingers).

category: Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed - Pharmacology (Neurosurgery)
question: Question #1154 [Bailey & Love Surgery 26th Ed]: Batch 1 - Question: A 22-year-old female with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus is started on an antihypertensive medication. 2 weeks later, she develops a dry, persistent cough without fever or dyspnea. Serum creatinine increases from 0.9 to 1.1 mg/dL.
option_a: Blockade of vascular smooth muscle L-type calcium channels causing vasodilation
option_b: Competitive inhibition of the Na+/Cl- cotransporter in the early distal convoluted tubule
option_c: Direct stimulation of central alpha-2 adrenergic receptors reducing sympathetic outflow
option_d: Selective antagonism of AT1 angiotensin receptors without affecting kinin metabolism
option_e: Inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme leading to impaired bradykinin breakdown
explanation: ACE inhibitors (e.g., lisinopril) prevent conversion of angiotensin I to II and block bradykinin degradation. Elevated bradykinin and substance P cause dry cough in ~10% of patients.
